title: Meta review: the 21 uncovered synthetic_reference finding records, plus a targeted check of 7 already covered - evidence re-derived, severities assessed, dispositions checked
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. The automated_review_status block below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Meta review of the finding records: for each record named in reviewed_ids, the claim was re-derived from the bytes it cites rather than read from the record, the severity was assessed, the disposition was checked against the normative vocabulary, and the record's own currency proof was verified to exist and to agree with the corpus. No finding record was modified by this pass. SECOND-READ CORRECTION MADE WITHIN THIS REVISION, BEFORE ISSUE. An earlier draft of the disposition for the withdrawn candidate FB2-REV-FND-000207 attributed the sentence 'a verifies link is a plan, not an outcome' to FB2-REV-FND-000008 to -000012. Reading those five records showed the sentence is in FB2-REV-FND-000001 to -000007 and not in -000008 to -000012, which instead carry an explicit RESIDUAL section naming FB2-REV-FND-000041 as the record that holds the open remainder. The disposition text was corrected to cite what is actually present. Recorded here rather than made silently: this record had not been issued when the correction was made, so it is folded into the revision-1 entry instead of manufacturing a revision-2 entry for a change no other record could have observed.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organisational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated.

scope: SCOPE: the finding records of the synthetic_reference profile. The 21 that no review record covered when this pass began, plus 7 already covered by FB2-REV-000013 and FB2-REV-000015 that were added because a defect spanning them was found during this pass; the targeted extent of the coverage of those 7 is stated in limitations and is deliberately narrow. The uncovered set was identified by an INDEPENDENT recomputation of the automated_review_coverage dimension, written from scratch and not importing corpus.py, which put the dimension at 190/285 with exactly 35 uncovered finding records, 21 of them in this profile and 14 in as_is. PROFILE IS EXPLICIT AND DELIBERATE: review.schema.json constrains reviewed_ids[].artifact_id to a three-segment id with additionalProperties false, so there is no profile field; naming both profiles' copies of one finding id would claim coverage of content this pass did not read. That is the defect recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000200 and as FB2-REV-FND-000046 for review records, so the as_is copies of the twelve paired records are covered by the sibling record FB2-REV-000022 and only the synthetic_reference copies appear here. Each record was read in full and its asserted condition re-derived from the corpus bytes it cites. This record does not review itself.

findings.description: Same defect as FB2-REV-FND-000198, seen from the other profile, and raised separately because a profile-scoped review may not bind one id to both profiles' content. FB2-REV-FND-000002 is scoped 'profile': 'synthetic_reference' and states that 'FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 in profile synthetic_reference is the target of 4 verifies link(s)', enumerating FB2-LNK-SAF-000021, FB2-LNK-SAF-000026, FB2-LNK-SAF-000042 and FB2-LNK-SAF-000049. Measured, synthetic_reference has THREE: FB2-LNK-SAF-000026, FB2-LNK-SAF-000042 and FB2-LNK-SAF-000049. FB2-LNK-SAF-000021 is added to the count but is an as_is record and carries no verifies link to FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 in this profile. The same over-count appears in FB2-REV-FND-000004 and FB2-REV-FND-000006 (4 claimed, 3 actual). THE VERDICTS ARE CORRECT AND ARE NOT DISTURBED: each record's asserted condition is 'this requirement has no verifies/validates link', each profile has at least one such link, so condition_still_holds=false is right, and the 'resolved' dispositions and the STALE audit_class stand. What is wrong is the count and the enumeration in the evidence - precisely the part a reader opens to check the claim. It is worth naming why this is not merely a stale number: link ids are per-profile, so FB2-LNK-SAF-000026 EXISTS in both profiles while FB2-LNK-SAF-000042 and -000049 exist only in synthetic_reference, and the same id means different relationships in different registries. A census summed without a profile key therefore cannot be checked by reading ids, which is presumably how the error survived a second read. NOT CORRECTED HERE: no finding record was modified by this pass.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the nine live link registries with the documented precedence order, de-duplicated by (profile, link_id). Inbound verifies/validates to FB2-SAF-FSR-000001: as_is = [FB2-LNK-SAF-000021] (1); synthetic_reference = [FB2-LNK-SAF-000026, FB2-LNK-SAF-000042, FB2-LNK-SAF-000049] (3). Claimed in the record: 4, being the union of the two profiles. Same shape for FSR-000002 (1 / 3, claimed 4) and FSR-000003 (1 / 3, claimed 4). FSR-000004 exists only in synthetic_reference and its record FB2-REV-FND-000007 is CORRECT at 3 of 3 - so the defect is present in 6 of the 12 records in the family, not in the family as a whole, and the 6 correct records (000007 to 000012) are recorded below as a performed check rather than claimed as evidence of a defect.

findings.description: The entire evidential basis of this record lies outside the distribution, so no reader of this repository can re-derive any of its numbers. FB2-REV-FND-000042 is severity high and disposition accepted - an OPEN finding - and every headline figure it states comes from three files under docs/artifacts/.work/: verification-env/sil/tools/find_vacuous_tests.py, verification-env/sil/logs/vacuous-final.json and verification-env/sil/VACUOUS-TESTS.md. That whole subtree is excluded from distribution and from the record population, three ways, all measured: 'git check-ignore -v docs/artifacts/.work' reports 'docs/artifacts/.gitignore:2:.work/'; 'git ls-files docs/artifacts/.work' returns ZERO tracked files; and corpus.py's iter_corpus_artifacts skips any path with '.work' in its parts, with a docstring saying evaluator-only is 'deliberately kept out of the record population'. docs/artifacts/.gitignore's own first line reads 'Temporary/local-only files excluded from distribution'. So on a clean checkout the cited files do not exist and the claims '82 of the 313 test files are vacuous', 'of the green files, 53 assert nothing and 192 carry a real assertion', '30 of those are build failures', 'the asserting count ROSE from 175 to 192', 'the vacuous green count also rose from 47 to 53' and '6 of the 23 tests that newly went from build failure to pass are themselves vacuous' are unverifiable - and unverifiable in the strict sense that the instrument that produced them is not in the repository either. This is not a new failure mode for this corpus; it is one it has already been bitten by and fixed once, and its own .gitignore records the precedent at length: 'A citation that names a file the distribution does not contain is a checkable claim that is false on a clean checkout: corpus.py check failed there with 14 evidence_file_missing findings that this working tree cannot reproduce, because the files were present' - fixed by re-including the logs rather than by rewriting the citation. THAT FIX DID NOT REACH THIS CASE, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: the fix works because execution records carry citations in evidence_files[], which corpus.py checks for existence. Finding records have no such slot. Measured across the whole family: 0 of 42 finding records carry evidence_files and 0 carry source_anchors, so every path a finding record cites is free text that no tool resolves. The corpus therefore cannot detect this class of error in a finding record even in principle, which is why it survived. The finding's own reasoning, its reading rule and its framing are careful and were NOT disturbed by this review; only its citability is defective. NOT CORRECTED HERE: no finding record was modified, and re-including .work/ is a repository-distribution decision, not a documentation fix.
findings.evidence: 'git check-ignore -v docs/artifacts/.work' -> 'docs/artifacts/.gitignore:2:.work/'. 'git ls-files docs/artifacts/.work | wc -l' -> 0. The three cited files exist in this working tree (VACUOUS-TESTS.md 9678 bytes, logs/vacuous-final.json 9831 bytes, tools/find_vacuous_tests.py 5052 bytes), so the defect is invisible here and visible only on a clean checkout - the same asymmetry the .gitignore comment describes for the 317 execution logs. corpus.py iter_corpus_artifacts skips '.work' by path part. Family-wide scan of all 42 records for the string 'docs/artifacts/.work': FB2-REV-FND-000034 (1 citation, names run.sh as the instrument used), FB2-REV-FND-000038 (1 citation, names a per-test log) and this record (3 citations, all load-bearing). Only this record's numbers depend on .work/ for their substance; the other two cite the instrument or a log alongside other evidence. Family-wide scan for machine-checked citation slots: evidence_files present on 0 of 42, source_anchors present on 0 of 42.

findings.description: Three records in this family file a block under the key 'reverification' that contains no re-verification. In 39 of the 42 finding records that block carries seven keys - date, method, audit_class, condition_still_holds, disposition_before, revision_before, evidence - and it is the corpus's proof-of-currency mechanism: a reader asks 'does this condition still hold?' and reads condition_still_holds, with audit_class to classify it and evidence to see the re-derivation. FB2-REV-FND-000039, FB2-REV-FND-000041 and FB2-REV-FND-000042 instead carry only date, method and 'raised_by': 'finding-closure pass over the 38 pre-existing records'. That is a provenance stamp of when the finding was RAISED, filed under the key the other 39 use for whether it is still TRUE. No condition_still_holds, no audit_class, no evidence, no disposition_before, no revision_before. The consequence is specific: a machine that decides currency by reading reverification.condition_still_holds finds the key absent on these three rather than false, and must special-case them; a human who assumes the key means the same thing in all 42 records reads 'raised_by' as if it were a verdict. The three affected records are not a random subset - they include two of the four severity-high records that remain OPEN (000041 and 000042, both disposition 'accepted'), and the one high record closed in this pass's own subject area (000039). THIS REVIEW DID THE MISSING WORK AND RECORDS THE RESULT, so the cost of the gap is visible rather than merely asserted. FB2-REV-FND-000041's substance was re-derived here and it HOLDS on every checkable claim: FB2-VER-TMS-000016..000020 exist with oracle_detail.kind of source_grounded, analytical_model, source_grounded, source_grounded and synthetic_assumption respectively, exactly as the record states; FB2-VER-EXE-000016..000020 all carry execution_kind 'none', outcome 'blocked' and a blocked_reason; all five FB2-SAF-SEC-* requirements carry verification_status 'not_verified' and a real_source_presence block; FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 exists and its own text describes the requirements as forward-engineered for a hypothetical project. FB2-REV-FND-000039's substance also holds: the '-FSR-' id filter is absent from the safety_requirement_completeness_checker in corpus.py, which now selects on declared type and declared domain, and the four self-tests that pin the widened scope (t_fault_reaction_rule_covers_sec_requirements, _still_covers_fsr_requirements, _respects_domain_boundary, _silent_when_field_present) are present in cmd_selftest. So the defect is in the meta-fields, not in the content - which is exactly why it is medium and not high, and why it is recorded against the records' own key rather than against their conclusions.
findings.evidence: Enumerated by reading the 'reverification' object of all 42 records in docs/artifacts/reviews/findings/: 39 carry {date, method, audit_class, condition_still_holds, disposition_before, revision_before, evidence}; 3 carry {date, method, raised_by} only - FB2-REV-FND-000039 (high, resolved), FB2-REV-FND-000041 (high, accepted), FB2-REV-FND-000042 (high, accepted). The 39 include every record dispositioned resolved, accepted or deferred that carries a currency proof, and the 'disposition_note' of the three exceptions states only that the record was filed against the vocabulary, with no claim that it was re-derived. Substance re-derived for FB2-REV-FND-000041 and FB2-REV-FND-000039 as set out in the description, from the artifact index and from docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py read as text.

findings.description: Seven records state their own disposition wrongly, in a field that now contradicts the field that carries it. FB2-REV-FND-000023 through FB2-REV-FND-000029 are all dispositioned 'resolved'. The lifecycle_status_note on each of the seven nonetheless ends: 'The disposition stays \'accepted\' because this schema has no closed value and the finding was valid: the acceptance stands and the closure is recorded in the resolution and revision history.' Two sentences are now false in all seven: the disposition does not stay 'accepted', it is 'resolved', and this schema does have a closed value - finding.schema.json's disposition enum carries 'resolved', with a normative definition in docs/artifacts/governance/finding-disposition-vocabulary.md. That is the same migration the seven records themselves record: the disposition_note of the records that DID migrate says so explicitly ('It was \'accepted\' before this revision, and that word was ambiguous'), and the sibling record FB2-REV-FND-000022 records the same migration in its resolution ('RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected... migrated to it'). So the seven were migrated in the disposition field and the explanatory note was left describing the pre-migration state. A reader who takes the note for the field learns that these seven are open acknowledgements, which is the precise confusion the migration was made to remove - 'accepted' was carrying at least three different jobs across this corpus... which left a reader unable to tell a closed finding from an open one by machine'. LOW AND NOT HIGHER, for three stated reasons: the machine-readable field is the correct one and the contradiction is in prose; no verdict, no severity and no evidence is affected; and a reader who reads the disposition field, which is what every tool in this corpus reads, gets the right answer. Recorded rather than corrected: these seven records were not modified by this pass.
findings.evidence: Read from the records. For each of FB2-REV-FND-000023, -000024, -000025, -000026, -000027, -000028 and -000029: disposition == 'resolved'; lifecycle_status_note contains the literal sentence "The disposition stays 'accepted' because this schema has no closed value". docs/artifacts/schemas/finding.schema.json disposition enum = [resolved, accepted, rejected, deferred, partial, in_progress], with 'resolved' documented as 'the asserted condition no longer holds and the record says so, with the fix named'. The 33 draft findings and the migrated records FB2-REV-FND-000001 to -000022 all state the migration in their own notes, so the seven are the only records where the note and the field disagree. 7 of 42 records affected; 35 of 42 clean.

dispositions.action: Accepted. Real evidence defect in three records of this profile (FB2-REV-FND-000002, -000004, -000006) and three in the sibling record FB2-REV-000022. Dispositions, audit_class and the false-condition verdicts are CORRECT in all six and are not disturbed; the per-profile count and link-id enumeration are wrong. NOT CORRECTED HERE: no finding record was modified. Referred to the finding-record owner.

Accepted, and referred rather than corrected, because the remedy is a distribution decision. FB2-REV-FND-000042 is an OPEN high-severity finding whose entire instrument and dataset live under a subtree that is git-ignored, untracked and excluded from the artifact index, so nothing about it can be re-derived from a clean checkout. No finding record was modified and .work/ was NOT re-included by this pass. Two things are needed and neither is a documentation edit: either the vacuous-test instrument and its output are moved somewhere the distribution carries, following the precedent the .gitignore comment records for the 317 execution logs, or the record's numbers are restated as asserted-by-a-session rather than as measured, so a reader is not told a measurement exists where the repository holds only a claim. Also referred to the schema owner: all 42 finding records lack evidence_files and source_anchors, so no tool can detect a citation to a non-distributed file in a finding record.

Accepted as a completeness defect in the meta-fields of three records (FB2-REV-FND-000039, -000041, -000042). This pass supplied the missing re-derivations rather than only reporting their absence: FB2-REV-FND-000041 and FB2-REV-FND-000039 were both re-derived from the corpus and BOTH HOLD, so the records' content is sound and only the currency proof is missing. NOT CORRECTED HERE: the three records were not modified, so their reverification blocks still lack condition_still_holds. Referred to the record owners, and referred to the schema owner as a family-level gap: the convention is not written down in finding.schema.json, which requires no reverification block at all, so nothing enforces that an OPEN finding carries one.

Accepted as a real internal contradiction in seven records, and NOT corrected: no finding record was modified by this pass. The fix is one sentence in each lifecycle_status_note, replacing the pre-migration claim about 'accepted' and 'no closed value' with the migration the other 15 migrated records already describe. Referred to the record owner. Severity low is deliberate and the reasoning is in the finding: the machine-readable field is correct, so no tool and no reader of the field is misled.

CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN ON A SECOND READ. Raised as a candidate and then withdrawn: 'FB2-REV-FND-000041 and -000042 are dispositioned 'accepted' with no remediation and no owner, which is itself suspicious.' NOT A DEFECT. Both carry owner_role 'data_quality_engineer', and both resolutions contain an explicit 'WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, precisely' section naming the work and the decision-maker: for -000041, a security test harness with a capture path and injection tooling plus a build of the service the requirements constrain, and for -000020's oracle an explicit statement that the honest disposition may be that the oracle is wrong rather than that the work is missing; for -000042, a per-file decision by someone who knows what each module must guarantee. Both also state why the work was not done and why doing it automatically would be fabrication. Withdrawn as a check that passed. The same check was applied to all 35 uncovered records: no record dispositioned accepted or deferred lacks an owner_role.

CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN ON A SECOND READ. Raised as a candidate and then withdrawn: 'FB2-REV-FND-000008 to -000012 are severity medium and resolved, while FB2-REV-FND-000041 covers the verification gap for the same five requirements at severity high - a severity inconsistency across the family.' NOT A DEFECT. The two sets of records assert different conditions and were correctly graded separately: 000008 to 000012 assert an absent verifies LINK, a structural condition that the rule fix genuinely closed, and each of those five carries an explicit RESIDUAL section stating that the LINK condition is resolved while the VERIFICATION condition is not, naming FB2-REV-FND-000041 as the record that carries the remainder. (An earlier draft of this disposition cited a different sentence - 'a verifies link is a plan, not an outcome' - which appears in the resolutions of FB2-REV-FND-000001 to -000007 and NOT in -000008 to -000012. The candidate was checked against the records on a second read, that citation was found to be wrong, and the withdrawal rests on the RESIDUAL sections that are actually present. The withdrawal itself is unaffected and is in fact better supported than the first draft claimed: naming the follow-on record explicitly is a stronger disclosure than a general caveat.) 000041 asserts the missing EVIDENCE and is correctly high. The family did the harder thing and refused to let the resolved records absorb the open remainder, which is what the disposition vocabulary requires. Withdrawn as a check that passed.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organisational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every record covered by this review, and for this review record itself. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No record covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit, and this review asserts none.

THIS IS A DIGEST ATTESTATION AND A RE-DERIVATION, NOT A RE-APPROVAL. Every digest in reviewed_ids was computed from the named file's bytes at the time of this pass, so it attests that the digest matches the file as it now stands. It does not attest that any human or any earlier review confirmed the content.
No finding record was modified by this pass. Where a finding record is defective, the defect is recorded here and in the dispositions below; repair is left to the record owner.

corpus.py was NOT modified. The metric and rule observations in this review were read from the tool's source; changing a tool or a metric in order to improve a reported number would be metric gaming and was avoided.

SCOPE LIMIT ON 7 OF THE 28 RECORDS, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: FB2-REV-FND-000023 to -000029 were already covered by FB2-REV-000013 and FB2-REV-000015, and are named here only because the defect raised as FB2-REV-FND-000205 spans all seven. For those seven this pass performed ONE check - whether lifecycle_status_note agrees with the disposition field - and read enough of each to state that check. It did NOT re-review their subjects, their evidence or their resolutions, and this record must not be cited as having done so. The 21 previously uncovered records were each read in full.

FB2-REV-FND-000042's numbers were NOT re-derived, because the instrument that produced them is under a subtree this repository does not distribute. That is the subject of FB2-REV-FND-000201 and is why this review reports the record as unverifiable rather than as wrong. Its internal arithmetic was checked and is self-consistent: 192 + 53 = 245 green, and 245/192 = 1.276, which is the 27 percent the record claims.

FB2-REV-FND-000031, -000032, -000039 and -000040 report on the corpus's own mutation and semantic-rule harness. Their claims about corpus.py were checked by reading the tool's source text and are accurate. Their claims about harness BEHAVIOUR - which mutations the detector set catches - were NOT re-run: that is the SIL harness's domain and this host's load average exceeded 380 throughout this pass. Those are recorded as asserted by the sessions that ran them.

Where a check came back clean it is recorded in results_summary and here, NOT in the findings arrays. Six of the twelve 'no verifies/validates link' records (FB2-REV-FND-000007 to -000012) were re-derived and are exactly right; every record dispositioned 'accepted' or 'deferred' carries an owner_role; FB2-REV-FND-000038's line references were confirmed correct; FB2-REV-FND-000022's lifecycle_status 'reviewed' is bounded by its own note. A review that listed those as findings would be padding.

This review raises no finding about the coverage metric itself. The prior defect recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000185 - a numerator computed from one hardcoded file - is no longer present: corpus.py lines 6182-6200 now aggregate reviewed_ids from every review record and union them with the reviewed_by links, and this review's own coverage contribution is therefore attributable. That is a check that passed and it is stated rather than claimed as a finding.

The four findings raised here are defects in the finding family's EVIDENCE, PROVENANCE, COMPLETENESS and INTERNAL CONSISTENCY. None alleges that a covered record reaches a wrong engineering conclusion; in FB2-REV-FND-000200 and -000205 the machine-readable fields are correct and only the supporting prose or enumeration is wrong, which is why those are medium and low rather than high.

results_summary.self_corrections_detail: One supporting citation in the withdrawn candidate FB2-REV-FND-000207 was wrong on first draft - it attributed the sentence 'a verifies link is a plan, not an outcome' to FB2-REV-FND-000008..000012, which do not contain it (it is in -000001..-000007). Found by reading the records rather than trusting the draft, and the disposition text was corrected in place. The withdrawal itself stands.

review_method: For each record named in reviewed_ids: (a) read the record in full; (b) re-derive its asserted condition from the corpus bytes it cites - the link registries with their documented precedence order, the artifact index read independently, docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py read as text, the link schema and the finding schema, and git's own index for what the distribution contains - rather than reading the condition off the record; (c) assess the severity against what the record asserts and what would follow from it being wrong; (d) check the disposition against docs/artifacts/governance/finding-disposition-vocabulary.md and the schema enum, and require an owner_role and a named closing action for anything not 'resolved'; (e) verify that a currency proof exists and agrees with the corpus, and supply the re-derivation personally where it does not. Family-wide structural scans (reverification key shape across all 42, lifecycle_status across all 42, .work citations across all 42, machine-checked citation slots across all 42) were run so that a defect could be sized rather than asserted. Coverage was computed by an independent script written from scratch for this pass, not by corpus.py.
